newsitem.title: USA: Grigsby firm campaign donations under probe--paper.
newsitem.headline: Grigsby firm campaign donations under probe--paper.

text.p: Federal investigators are probing whether a firm owned by California bond underwriter Calvin Grigsby used Port of Miami money to make campaign contributions to a former Missouri politician, the Miami Herald said Friday.
One of Grigsby's companies, Fiscal Operations, has a contract to manage Dade County's cargo crane operations at the county-run seaport.

The newspaper said the investigators are reviewing the financial records of Fiscal Operations, specifically the $8,000 it contributed to the campaign of former St. Louis comptroller Virvus Jones in the early 1990s. Jones resigned in 1995 after pleading guilty to tax fraud for failing to report money siphoned from his campaign accounts.
Federal prosecutors said they could not comment, and neither Grigsby nor his attorney, Carl Douglas, could be reached for comment.
The newspaper said Grigsby himself also contributed $49,956 to Jones' campaign between 1991 and 1993, and that investigators had questioned Jones about whether the donations were bribes.
Grigsby hired Jones' daughter at his municipal bond firm, formerly known as Grigsby Brandford & Co, which underwrote bonds for several St. Louis projects.

Quoting Jones' attorney, Donald Wolff, the newspaper said U.S. attorneys and FBI agents questioned Jones in prison late last year, and that Jones told them the contributions came with no strings attached.
Wolff said Jones gave Grigsby's firm bond business because he wanted minorities to receive a bigger share of city business.
"Virvus (Jones) has never taken a payoff in his life," Wolff told the newspaper.
The Herald said the probe is part of Operation Greenpalm, an ongoing investigation of alleged public finance corruption in Miami and Dade County.

Fiscal Operations has a 20-year contract to manage the Port of Miami's gantry cranes. The Herald reported in October that it had spent thousands of dollars of public money on entertainment, a charity golf tournamanet and a $20,000 contribution to the Democratic National Committee.
The firm agreed to reimburse the county for the Democratic Committee contribution after the newspaper reported it.

Fiscal Operations' contract runs through June 1, 2002 and gives Port Director Carmen Lunetta unilateral control over how much the company is paid and how it spends port money. Lunetta said he did not approve the political contributions, but did approve the others expenses because they helped promote the port or supported good causes.
Fiscal Operations is paid an annual management fee of $150,000 plus expenses for maintaining the cranes and billing shipping companies that use them. Grigsby also receives a $75,000 annual salary.

he port's gantry cranes generated $7.8 million in billings last year. The seaport got about $1 million and the rest went to Fiscal Operations for maintenance, stevedore salaries, office help and travel and promotions expenses, the newspaper said.
